topic.topic: Why a lunar month is longer than the Moon’s orbit
topic.angle: Explain why the Moon completes an orbit in about 27.3 days but takes about 29.5 days to return to the same phase: while the Moon orbits Earth, Earth also moves along its orbit around the Sun, so the Moon must travel a little farther to restore the same Sun-Earth-Moon alignment.

decisions.reason: A clear, evergreen explanation supported by the retrieved NASA sources, distinct from the archived eclipse and daytime-visibility articles.
NASA’s retrieved Moon Phases page supports both periods and explains that the longer phase cycle reflects the Moon’s motion relative to the Sun; the topic is ready to draft.
The draft’s key periods and explanation are supported by the retrieved NASA sources; an independent factual review is the next step.
